characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements for every material state
performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction by grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques

interfaces.interface_notes: For the intermediate 2–6 wt.% Al variants, the aging-induced κ-carbide strengthening effect is much weaker than for the ~8 wt.% Al variant.

phase_interfaces.coherence: ordered fcc; lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to the austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix, enabling cuboidal nanoprecipitates

interfaces.slip_behavior: After aging at 500–600 °C, twinning is reduced and strain hardening is essentially associated with κ-carbide and solid-solution strengthening.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Aging response: the 6 wt.% Al variant is only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of mechanical data, compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening).
Intermediate 2–6 wt.% Al variants do not show equivalent mechanical properties compared with the ~8 wt.% Al variant, and show a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Melting and casting in a VIM furnace under 400 mbar Ar pressure; system modified to synthesize five different alloys in one operation using five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace, filled successively from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10 × 50 × 130 mm³ blocks were hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Sheets were reheated to 1100 °C, water quenched, and cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments (2 × 60 × 55 mm³) for each alloy composition.
Homogenization performed at 1100 °C for 2 h under Ar, followed by water quenching.
Aging conducted in air at 500 °C for 1 h, followed by oil quenching (one of the 450/500/550/600 °C × 0/1/24 h RAP heat-treatment matrix).
Scales were removed from the surfaces after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile testing at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1; all plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized microstructure with grain size ~20 µm and some retained microsegregations of Mn (after hot rolling and water quenching).

unmapped_findings: The yield strength of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al sample is not numerically resolved for the 500 °C/1 h condition in the text: Fig. 3(a) shows YS stays between roughly 350 and 450 MPa from 0Al to 4Al and then climbs steeply toward the 900 MPa gridline at 8Al, with the 450 °C/1 h curve dipping to its minimum at 6Al (block_id: figure_003, b0022, b0028).

Mass density at ~6 wt.% Al in the Fe-Mn-Al-C alloy series is about 7.15 g/cm³ (Fig. 1), with density falling from ~7.15 g/cm³ at 6 wt.% Al to ~6.4 g/cm³ at 13 wt.% Al; no specific printed density value is given for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al alloy itself (block_id: figure_001, b0011).

General κ-carbide description relevant to aged Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys: Al promotes the formation of nanoprecipitates upon aging with L′1₂ structure and approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)3AlC; these κ-carbides have an ordered fcc structure with lattice mismatch below 3% relative to the austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix and can form cuboidal nanoprecipitates. For the 6 wt.% Al intermediate variant, however, the aging-induced strengthening effect is reported as weak (block_id: b0015, b0024, b0025).
